Codex review: needs real behavior proof before merge. _Reviewed September 5, 2026, 10:58 AM ET / 14:58 UTC._ # ClawSweeper review ## What this changes Enforces the transcript byte limit during heartbeats and adds fenced Codex host compaction with atomic accounting, documentation, and Gateway regression coverage. ## Merge readiness ⛔ **Blocked before merge - 3 items remain** This repair remains necessary on current main. The previous wording finding is resolved, and no new blocking code defect was found; the captured proof still does not cover the final atomic-persistence restart boundary. **Priority:** P1 **Reviewed head:** `ec44630c4ecb4d2a2ab588fda5f490154a379ac8` ## Review scores | Measure | Result | What it means | |---|---|---| | **Overall readiness** | 🦐 gold shrimp **(3/6)** | A coherent repair with useful regression coverage, pending proof for the final persistence boundary. | | **Proof confidence** | 🦐 gold shrimp **(3/6)** | Needs stronger real behavior proof before merge: The captured AWS built-Gateway run at 4ee3a708 supports heartbeat compaction, restricted native rejection, and stale-writer fencing. The final SQLite transaction and pre-checkpoint restart case have no matching observed result in the supplied evidence; the earlier restart row records one native request where the current case requires zero. After adding proof, update the PR body; ClawSweeper should re-review automatically. If it does not, the PR author or someone with repository write access can comment `@clawsweeper re-review`. | | **Patch quality** | 🐚 platinum hermit **(4/6)** | No actionable review findings were identified. | ## Verification | Check | Result | Evidence | |---|---|---| | **Real behavior** | Needs proof | Needs stronger real behavior proof before merge: The captured AWS built-Gateway run at 4ee3a708 supports heartbeat compaction, restricted native rejection, and stale-writer fencing. The final SQLite transaction and pre-checkpoint restart case have no matching observed result in the supplied evidence; the earlier restart row records one native request where the current case requires zero. After adding proof, update the PR body; ClawSweeper should re-review automatically. If it does not, the PR author or someone with repository write access can comment `@clawsweeper re-review`. | | **Evidence reviewed** | 10 items | Current main still contains the reported bypass: At the fetched main revision, runSessionCompactionIfNeeded returns for isHeartbeat before resolving maxActiveTranscriptBytes. The current documented byte guard promises semantic compaction before another run.
Host persistence boundary: The admission owner supplies a persistence callback that commits the compaction event, count, and byte latch together. The SQLite owner validates the appended event and rechecks writer/lifecycle ownership before updating the session row.
Entry points, authority, and sibling behavior: Read the direct-reply and follow-up admission callers, queued compaction, runtime delegate, direct compactor, transcript guard, and accounting owner. The private claim is one-shot and target-bound; transcript writes revalidate the captured writer. Heartbeats skip token maintenance, while CLI/native-transcript owners retain their existing exclusion. | | **Findings** | None | None. | | **Security** | None | None. | ## How this fits together Heartbeat and chat admission check OpenClaw’s stored conversation before starting another turn. Host compaction summarizes that transcript, while the Codex plugin separately controls its native conversation. ```mermaid flowchart TD A[Heartbeat or chat turn] --> B[Read active transcript size] B --> C{Byte limit reached and unlatched?} C -->|No| G[Admit next turn] C -->|Yes| D[Validate session and writer] D --> E[Compact host transcript and commit accounting] E --> F[Optional eligible Codex synchronization] F --> G ``` ## Before merge - [ ] **Add real behavior proof** - Needs stronger real behavior proof before merge: The captured AWS built-Gateway run at 4ee3a708 supports heartbeat compaction, restricted native rejection, and stale-writer fencing. The final SQLite transaction and pre-checkpoint restart case have no matching observed result in the supplied evidence; the earlier restart row records one native request where the current case requires zero. After adding proof, update the PR body; ClawSweeper should re-review automatically. If it does not, the PR author or someone with repository write access can comment `@clawsweeper re-review`. - [ ] **Resolve merge risk (P1)** - The final atomic persistence path lacks captured crash/restart results; an interruption could otherwise leave compaction accounting or retry suppression inconsistent with the committed transcript. - [ ] **Complete next step (P2)** - Provide results from the existing Gateway restart scenario against the final atomic-persistence code and align the PR’s checkpoint/native-request evidence with those observations.

### Review metrics | Metric | Value | Why it matters | |---|---|---| | **Production versus regression coverage** | Production net +358; tests and QA support net +2,789 | Growth adds private authority and atomic persistence boundaries; shared accounting was moved into one reusable projection rather than duplicated. | ### Root-cause cluster Relationship: `fixed_by_candidate` Canonical: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/136452 Summary: This PR is the candidate repair for the heartbeat byte-cap bypass; related Codex work overlaps only part of the behavior. Members: - `canonical`: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/136452 - The open report establishes the heartbeat bypass and is explicitly linked by this PR. - `partial_overlap`: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/137752 - Addresses rejected Codex turns through benign-decline classification, without the same host-transcript enforcement. - `adjacent_distinct`: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/137914 - The closed report concerns native binding continuity after host generation rotation. - `adjacent_distinct`: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/138184 - Closed unmerged generation-transition work is not a replacement landing path. Proposal only: this assessment does not dispatch repair, suppress jobs, mutate sibling items, close, or merge anything. ### Merge-risk options **Maintainer options:** 1. **Verify the final interruption boundary (recommended)** Refresh the existing Gateway scenario evidence to demonstrate atomic persistence and successor continuity after interruption before checkpoint creation. ### Technical review Best possible solution: Keep one semantic compaction pipeline with atomic transcript/accounting commits and proven restart recovery; the private authority and transaction boundaries justify growth beyond a guard-only fix. Do we have a high-confidence way to reproduce the issue? Yes, from source: heartbeat admission returns before reading the configured byte cap on current main. The discussion supplies earlier before/after Gateway observations; this review executed no runtime reproduction. Is this the best way to solve the issue? Yes at the owner boundary: reusing semantic host compaction preserves the byte guard, whereas accepting native declines alone leaves host growth unresolved. Final persistence recovery still needs observed proof. AGENTS.md: found and applied where relevant. Codex review notes: model internal, reasoning high; reviewed against [0f54c8698228](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/0f54c8698228fc1c7564db4e0a1a21819cba9be5). ### Labels Label justifications: - `P1`: The linked report describes heartbeat-driven transcript growth and Gateway OOM crashes, and current main still contains the bypass. - `merge-risk: 🚨 session-state`: The new transcript/count/latch transaction needs observed recovery across its final pre-checkpoint crash boundary. - `rating: 🦐 gold shrimp`: Overall readiness is 🦐 gold shrimp; proof is 🦐 gold shrimp and patch quality is 🐚 platinum hermit. - `status: 📣 needs proof`: The PR needs real behavior proof before ClawSweeper can clear the contributor ask. The final SQLite transaction and pre-checkpoint restart case have no matching observed result in the supplied evidence; the earlier restart row records one native request where the current case requires zero. After adding proof, update the PR body; ClawSweeper should re-review automatically. If it does not, the PR author or someone with repository write access can comment `@clawsweeper re-review`. ### Evidence What I checked: - **Current main still contains the reported bypass:** At the fetched main revision, runSessionCompactionIfNeeded returns for isHeartbeat before resolving maxActiveTranscriptBytes. The current documented byte guard promises semantic compaction before another run. ([`src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-memory.ts:721`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/0f54c8698228fc1c7564db4e0a1a21819cba9be5/src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-memory.ts#L721), [0f54c8698228](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/0f54c8698228fc1c7564db4e0a1a21819cba9be5)) - **Host persistence boundary:** The admission owner supplies a persistence callback that commits the compaction event, count, and byte latch together. The SQLite owner validates the appended event and rechecks writer/lifecycle ownership before updating the session row. ([`src/config/sessions/session-accessor.sqlite-transcript-write.ts:353`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/ec44630c4ecb4d2a2ab588fda5f490154a379ac8/src/config/sessions/session-accessor.sqlite-transcript-write.ts#L353), [ec44630c4ecb](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/ec44630c4ecb4d2a2ab588fda5f490154a379ac8)) - **Entry points, authority, and sibling behavior:** Read the direct-reply and follow-up admission callers, queued compaction, runtime delegate, direct compactor, transcript guard, and accounting owner. The private claim is one-shot and target-bound; transcript writes revalidate the captured writer. Heartbeats skip token maintenance, while CLI/native-transcript owners retain their existing exclusion. ([`src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/transcript-byte-preflight-authority.ts:61`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/ec44630c4ecb4d2a2ab588fda5f490154a379ac8/src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/transcript-byte-preflight-authority.ts#L61), [ec44630c4ecb](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/ec44630c4ecb4d2a2ab588fda5f490154a379ac8)) - **Codex dependency signal and preserved restriction:** The changed docs explicitly describe secondary thread/compact/start synchronization. The actual Codex plugin rejects host-isolated and restricted bindings before client acquisition; host compaction does not remove that restriction. ([`extensions/codex/src/app-server/compact.ts:501`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/ec44630c4ecb4d2a2ab588fda5f490154a379ac8/extensions/codex/src/app-server/compact.ts#L501), [ec44630c4ecb](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/ec44630c4ecb4d2a2ab588fda5f490154a379ac8)) - **Direct upstream contract inspection:** Verified repository ownership through the sibling checkout’s backing cache origin, https://github.com/openai/codex.git. Personally inspected thread.rs:1113-1120, thread_processor.rs:2347-2359, and session/handlers.rs:246-251,675-677: the request contains a thread ID, checks direct-input permission, submits Op::Compact, and returns an empty acknowledgement; the compaction task runs separately. ([`codex-rs/app-server/src/request_processors/thread_processor.rs:2347`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/3d2ee51ca2d5db578f328aa75e20aa22c0197c9a/codex-rs/app-server/src/request_processors/thread_processor.rs#L2347), [3d2ee51ca2d5](https://github.com/openai/codex/commit/3d2ee51ca2d5db578f328aa75e20aa22c0197c9a)) - **Captured proof retains useful earlier coverage:** The complete supplied body, captured under sourceRevision 5c3d446333593c07f4439d35da4f6a1fbc86357e72a5c67e510d4f291f82dcdc, identifies AWS built-Gateway proof at 4ee3a708. It reports fresh/restricted continuation, native rejection, and substituted/revoked writers rejected before provider traffic or transcript commits. Its restart row records one native compact request, unlike the current pre-checkpoint scenario. Exact-head Codex owner-boundary proof completed on
`bf0d7d489021df6c594478101f2706a322e97103`.

Command:

`node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/codex/src/app-server/compact.test.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/startup-binding.test.ts`

Result: 2 files passed, 93/93 tests passed.

The focused run directly covers the remaining ClawSweeper authority concerns:

- restricted native authority and host-isolated operations return without any
  `thread/compact/start` request;
- admitted authority rotating while queued rejects before client acquisition,
  with both `clientFactory` and app-server request calls remaining zero;
- a recovered predecessor rotating during startup rejects before native
  compaction and preserves its binding;
- the startup matrix covers byte and token pressure under expected, ordinary,
  and revoked ownership, preserving the binding for rejected or revoked claims.

This supplements the fresh exact-head Crabbox proof in the PR body. It does not
reuse proof from run 697 or another superseded head.
